method: Built-in imagegen, new full-body animation poses derived from the approved Legendary references. Previously completed artwork is untouched. No completed Batch 5 atlas checkpoint was present.

prompts.sonic1: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet, not a concept card. Reference image defines Sonic Tusk: massive elephant/mammoth beast with four connected weight-bearing legs, dark blue/steel armor with gold trim, bright blue eyes, long segmented trunk, two huge curved ivory tusks, gold mechanical armor fittings. Preserve that identity and detailed inked comic-book shading. Create 16 DISTINCT full-body poses in a STRICT 4-column by 4-row evenly spaced grid, on genuinely transparent RGBA background, no words, no borders. Camera side three-quarter facing RIGHT consistently. Each pose fully contained in its cell, including tusks and trunk. Use small enough scale to leave generous transparent gaps on all four sides; no neighboring poses/effects may overlap. Equal standing body size and common ground line per row. Row 1 four subtle breathing idle poses with trunk motion. Row 2 four walking-cycle poses, alternating planted feet and weight shifting, all four legs connected. Row 3 directional sonic blast: anticipation, trunk and head drawn back charging, head/trunk thrust forward with compact blue sound pulse, recovery. Row 4 tusk strike: low anticipation, head reared slightly, decisive forward/upward tusk sweep, recovery. Do not crop or copy miniature reference poses; author complete new articulated poses. No new weapons, no background, no ground shadow. Keep sonic effects compact within the cell.
prompts.sonic2: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a SQUARE production transparent RGBA sprite sheet for Sonic Tusk. Reference 1 is approved identity, reference 2 is the already created animation design to match exactly: quadruped armored mammoth, four attached legs, long trunk, two curved ivory tusks, blue-black steel and gold armor, blue eyes. Same detailed comic outlines/shading and right-facing three-quarter camera. 16 full-body poses, STRICT FOUR COLUMNS AND FOUR ROWS of equal SQUARE cells. Each whole pose occupies ONLY central 65% of its cell; at least 15% EMPTY TRANSPARENT margin on EVERY side. Do not let tusks, trunk, tail, or effects touch neighboring cells. No text or scenery or ground shadows. Same body scale in all 16 cells. Row 1 expanding sonic wave: prepare, charge trunk inward, emit compact blue circular sound ripple from forward trunk, recover. Row 2 tusk charging: lowered ready stance, crouched launch, powerful forward running stride with tusks ahead and planted/pushing hind feet, recover and brake. Row 3 powerful phase-three layered sonic attack: head/trunk back, intense charge, two compact concentric blue sound arcs directly ahead, recover. Row 4 tusk combo: windup left shoulder low, head coils up, sweeping upward strike with trunk controlled and tusks unmistakable, recovery. No new weapons or mechanics. Draw distinct poses, keep anatomy and armor stable. Effects limited to small local accents; full world projectiles are rendered by existing game code.
prompts.sonic3: Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent PNG production sprite sheet for Sonic Tusk, matching the supplied completed design exactly: quadrupedal mammoth with four connected legs, enormous ivory tusks, segmented trunk, blue-black and gold mechanical armor, blue eyes, inked detailed comic shading. Eight full-body poses, FOUR COLUMNS by TWO ROWS. Face RIGHT at same three-quarter angle. Equal standing scale across all poses; keep entire body/tusks/tail inside its cell with broad empty transparent gutters. No text, no background, no shadow. Row 1 HIT reaction sequence: flinch with eyes narrowed, recoil weight on rear legs, lower head and brace feet, recover standing. Row 2 DEFEAT sequence: legs buckle, body falls sideways while trunk lowers, body on ground with legs folded and armor still connected, completely collapsed motionless mammoth with trunk curled on ground and both tusks visible. Defeat must actually get much shorter in height, never resize character smaller to simulate collapse. Maintain anatomy and armor continuity. Do not add gore, weapons, scenery, or effects. These are NEW separate animation poses, not reference thumbnails.
prompts.styro1: Use case: stylized-concept. Create production animation sprites of Dr. Styro using this approved reference EXACTLY as identity: humanoid armored scientist, pale white angular helmet/crest, black gas-mask respirator, round luminous green goggles, white/dark metal suit with gold edging, broad chemical apparatus backpack with blue/green canisters and tubes, large mechanical gloves, two arms/two legs. Do NOT substitute a generic lab-coat scientist, do not add a gun or new weapon. Detailed inked comic-book shading matching reference. Transparent RGBA PNG, no scenery, text, grid lines or shadows. SIXTEEN distinct full-body poses in FOUR COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, preferably a square sheet. Side three-quarter camera facing RIGHT. Whole character and all tubes remain within each cell with generous transparent gutters, equal body scale/foot baselines. Row 1 idle four breathing/weight shifts with subtle apparatus motion. Row 2 four walking strides with connected knees and planted feet. Row 3 bouncing styrofoam attack: crouch preparation, glove brought back holding a small white foam orb, underarm forward toss with small orb at glove, recovery. Row 4 straight foam shot: arms prepare, glove charged, forward arm thrust firing a compact white foam pulse, recovery. No extraneous huge effects; character must be complete and separated in every cell. Author real new poses, not miniature reference crops.
prompts.styro2: Use case: stylized-concept. Dr. Styro game sprites, exactly match the approved identity in reference 1 and new animation model in reference 2: white crested helmet, black respirator, green round goggles, colorful chemical backpack canisters and tubes, white/black/gold mechanical scientist suit and purple/blue gloves. Two connected arms and legs. SAME comic shading and proportions. Transparent RGBA sheet, 4 COLUMNS x 4 ROWS, 16 new full-body poses, facing RIGHT three-quarter. Equal body scale, grounded feet, generous empty margins between whole characters. NO text/scenery/ground shadows. Row 1 temporary foam-barrier deployment: hands gather, open palms, forward palms with small white foam plates immediately ahead, lower arms recovery. Row 2 mechanical-trap activation: glance toward wrist controls, finger hovers, press wrist control while other hand points toward ground, recovery. Row 3 laboratory-machinery activation: low ready pose, hand lifts to shoulder, arm raised decisively as command to existing arena machines, recovery. Do NOT draw new weapons or big machines on the sprite. Row 4 foam volley: prepare both gloves, charge small foam pellets at hands, both hands project several small foam pieces, recover. Keep effects compact INSIDE cell and avoid overlap. Preserve full backpack, boots, gloves and helmet in each frame; do not crop anything. No generic lab coat or new equipment.
prompts.styro3: Use case: stylized-concept. Eight transparent full-body Dr. Styro animation poses in a FOUR COLUMN by TWO ROW grid. Match supplied finished sprite identity exactly: white high crested helmet, round green goggles and black respirator, white/black/gold armored scientist with connected chemical backpack tubes and blue/red/green canisters, purple gloves, two arms two legs. Detailed bold inked comic shading. Camera three-quarter facing RIGHT. Equal body scale; preserve armor/helmet/canisters between poses. Broad transparent gutters and no overlap, no cropping, no text, background or ground shadow. Row1 four HIT reaction poses: flinch, recoil leaning back with feet braced, crouched recovery, regain upright stance. Row2 four DEFEAT poses: stagger with sagging arms, knees buckle with backpack tilting, fall onto side with connected limbs, lie fully collapsed on side, helmet and apparatus intact and dim goggles. Last pose is much lower and wider, not a standing figure shrunk. No gore, no new equipment. All complete full-body poses inside individual cells. Do not copy miniature concept poses.
prompts.wastelander1: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game animation sprite sheet for LEGENDARY Wastelander, using the supplied approved character exactly: massive muscular armored desert outlaw, broad dark cowboy hat with gold trim, orange/rust skin and armor, dark black-brown leather outfit and boots, gold skull chest emblem, heavy armored gauntlets, rugged masked face/respirator and belt chains. NOT a sludge creature or green swamp monster. No guns or new weapons. Detailed bold comic-book inks and shading. Transparent RGBA background with no scenery/text/shadow. SIXTEEN full-body poses in strict FOUR COLUMNS x FOUR ROWS, same right-facing three-quarter camera and body size. Broad transparent gutters; keep every hat, glove, chain and boot entirely within its cell. Row1 four idle breathing/weight-shift poses. Row2 four heavy walking strides with planted boots and flexing knees. Row3 powerful punch sequence: braced anticipation, rear fist pulled back, heavy forward punch, recovery. Row4 toxic projectile sequence: prepare forward gauntlet, small yellow-green toxin glow at glove, extend arm with compact toxic pulse leaving palm, recovery. All distinct newly authored poses, not cropped miniatures. Keep face, hat, costume and muscular proportions stable, no extra limbs. Full moving projectiles are rendered separately by the existing game.
prompts.wastelander2: Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent game animation sheet, LEGENDARY Wastelander, matching reference 1 approved design and reference 2 authored sprites exactly: massive orange/rust muscular outlaw with broad dark gold-trimmed cowboy hat, black/brown and gold armor, skull emblem, belt chains, heavy gauntlets and boots, rugged masked face. NOT Sludge Beast. Detailed comic ink shading, two arms/two legs, facing RIGHT three-quarter throughout. FOUR COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS: 16 distinct whole-body poses of the SAME scale. Wide transparent empty gutters around every cell; effects and hats/feet cannot overlap neighbors. No text, scenery, ground shadows, guns or new weapons. Row1 toxic shockwave: brace legs, draw both arms inward, push arms outward with a small yellow-green ground ripple, recovery. Row2 heavy ground slam: crouch, raise one gauntlet overhead, smash fist to ground with compact local impact, recover from crouch. Row3 Phase3 toxic-ground hazards: prepare, gauntlet gathers green toxin, press gauntlet into ground with small local fumes, recover. Row4 Phase3 toxic combo: gather strength, twist torso preparing both fists, forceful low sweeping arm action with two small yellow-green arcs, recover. Full world hazards already exist in game; only animate body and compact local accents. Do not create extra attack types.
prompts.wastelander3: Use case: stylized-concept. Eight newly authored production animation sprites for LEGENDARY Wastelander matching supplied finished character exactly: muscular orange/rust outlaw, broad black gold-trimmed cowboy hat, dark leather and gold armored suit with skull chest emblem, belt chains, massive gauntlets and boots. Preserve face and hat identity, no guns and no sludge form. Transparent RGBA, FOUR COLUMNS TWO ROWS, full-body three-quarter facing RIGHT. Same scale in all cells and generous transparent gutters, no text/scenery/shadows. Row1 HIT sequence: flinch with shoulders raised, recoil with torso leaning back and boots braced, crouch/recover, steady ready stance. Row2 DEFEAT sequence: stagger lowering fists, knees buckle and hat tilts while still attached, fall onto side with connected limbs, lie fully collapsed on ground with hat still recognizable. Final body much lower and wider, not a small standing pose. All hands, boots, chains and hat fit wholly inside each cell; no adjacent overlaps. Keep detailed comic-book ink outlines and shading, no gore.

packing: Deterministic alpha-component isolation, uniform per-sheet sizing and foot anchoring. Source rectangles and hashes are in batch5-atlas-manifest.json. World projectiles and hazards remain in the original renderer.
limitations: Four poses per sequence with short non-contact blends; not dense hand-drawn animation.
Fine generated armor and chain details vary slightly between poses.
